chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said:

If a man forgets one sajdah and is certain that he omitted it, then he should perform it after he sits, before he gives salām. But if he is doubtful, then he should give salām, then perform it, and let him recite a light tashahhud. And he should not call it a peck, for the peck is the peck of the crow.

key_terms.الْغُرَابِ: the crow, used here as a comparison for improper hurried movement
key_terms.تَشَهُّدًا خَفِيفًا: a brief recitation of the tashahhud
key_terms.شَاكًّا: being in a state of doubt or uncertainty
key_terms.يُسَلِّمَ: to give salām ending the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets one sajdah in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who omits a single sajdah in salat (prayer). It distinguishes between certainty and doubt regarding the omission, and it also instructs that the sajdah should be performed properly and not in a hurried, pecking manner.
